Hey Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Helpful discussion. A couple of items we wanted to confirm on the usage/pricing side so we can scope procurement and the POC: 

- Expected steady monthly tokens: we ballparked 30M–50M (mostly completions-heavy for user messages, ~60% completions / 40% prompt).
- Peak concurrency: during promotional spikes we can see bursts — rough upper bound ~450 tps for short windows, typical peak ~250 tps.
- Budget target: our finance lead suggested a target of ~$13 / 1M tokens but willing to consider a committed price if the unit economics move the dial.
- SLA ask: 99th percentile tail latency target around 150–200ms for single-turn chat.

Can you confirm whether Redwood hosted API pricing and burst capacity can support the above shape, and what a conservative $/1M estimate looks like at 30M vs 50M commit? Also: any special considerations for streaming vs non-streaming traffic?

If easier, happy to hop on a short call tomorrow AM.

—Elena

Elena — great notes and clear profile. Short answers up front: Redwood Hosted can support that shape; pricing depends on committed slab, token mix, and streaming ratio. I attached a quick consumption workbook (see attachment) that sketches a few scenarios. High-level ballpark for hosted API:

- No commit / pay-as-you-go: ~ $17 / 1M tokens (retail, includes burst overhead)
- Mid commit (30M/mo): ~ $14–15 / 1M tokens
- Higher commit (40–50M/mo): ~ $11.5–13 / 1M tokens (steeper discounts if multi-quarter commit)

Notes and caveats:
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming has the same token accounting but slightly higher egress/operational cost; if >30% of traffic is streaming we model a ~5–8% uplift on the unit price unless we agree on a usage mix carve-out.
- Peak TPS: we can handle short bursts to 450–600 tps if we configure burst capacity, but that ties up burst pool and influences pricing commitments. If you want a hard SLA for 600 tps sustained we should talk Dedicated or a written burst reservation.
- Latency: 99th percentile of 150–200ms is aggressive for some models; we can meet that on smaller context windows and optimized model variants — need to confirm model choice.

Action items I'm proposing:
1) Karthik — can you draft a committed slab option (40M) with a $/1M table and burst allowance?
2) Elena — can you share a simple token-split sample (two days of normal + peak hour) so we can model mixing effects?
3) I'll drop the consumption workbook referenced here: novapulse_consumption_estimate.xlsx and a HubSpot note linking the POC requirements.

Happy to take a quick call tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jonas / Marissa — looping in pricing details and a suggested commercial. Draft numbers below (internal):

- Suggested committed slab: 40M tokens / month for 12 weeks POC-to-pilot conversion window. Price: $12.50 / 1M tokens.
- Overshoot / burst allowance: 10% free burst (managed) then overage at $16 / 1M until next slab threshold.
- If they commit to 3-month minimum of 40M, we can hold $11.50 / 1M for months 2–3 as an incentive.
- Streaming uplift: +6% on unit price if streaming >30% unless they shift to a lower-latency model variant we pre-approve.

Operational notes:
- For peaks up to 600 tps: approve burst pool — cost modeled into the slab but we should flag that sustained >5 min at 600 tps needs Dedicated.
- SLA language for 99th pct: we can include a target but exclude model-variant regressions and customer-side network constraints.

I'll attach the updated slab pdf (pricing-slabs-v2.pdf) and recommend we present the 40M / $12.5 scenario as our commercial starting point.

—Karthik

- Our working expectation for the POC: steady-state ~35M tokens/mo, peaks up to ~600 tps during marketing pushes (those spikes are usually <10 minutes).
- Token mix: roughly 55% completions / 45% prompts; streaming is about ~10% of requests (mostly live chat).
- Budget: finance is comfortable with $13 / 1M as a stretch target. The 40M @ $12.50 looks reasonable if we can get a simple 30-day exit clause post-POC and an explicit burst allowance for the first 2 months.
